tasks.objective: Create internal/next/contract/types.go with all exported core types: SpecScenario{Name, Given, When, Then, Notes string}, ScenarioContract{Scenarios []ScenarioAssertions}, ScenarioAssertions{Name string, Assertions []ContractAssertion}, ContractAssertion{FileExists string, FileContains *FileContainsAssertion, FileNotModified string, FileNotExists string, FileNotContains *FileContainsAssertion} with yaml omitempty tags, FileContainsAssertion{Path, Pattern string}, ContractFailure{ScenarioName, AssertionType, Details string}. Package is 'contract'. Include a package doc comment.

Create internal/next/contract/parse.go with exported func ParseScenarios(content string) []SpecScenario. Parse spec markdown by scanning for lines beginning with '### Scenario:' to find scenario boundaries. For each scenario block, extract: Name from the header (strip '### Scenario: ' prefix), and Given/When/Then/Notes blocks by matching '**Given:**', '**When:**', '**Then:**', '**Notes:**' labels (collect text until next label or next '### Scenario:' header). Skip scenarios missing BOTH When and Then (log warning to stderr). Given and Notes are optional. Return only valid scenarios.

Create internal/next/contract/parse_test.go with TestParseScenarios tests covering: (1) happy path — 2 valid scenarios with all blocks, correct Name/Given/When/Then/Notes extracted; (2) empty input returns empty slice; (3) scenario missing both When and Then is excluded from result; (4) scenario with When but no Then is excluded; (5) scenario with Then but no When is excluded; (6) Notes block optional — scenario included without it; (7) Given block optional — scenario included without it; (8) mix of valid and invalid scenarios — only valid ones returned.

Create internal/next/contract/evaluator.go with: (1) a GitRunner interface or func type for running 'git diff --name-only HEAD -- <path>' so the evaluator is testable without a real git repo; (2) FileSystemEvaluator struct with workDir string and a gitRunner func; (3) NewFileSystemEvaluator(workDir string) constructor using real git execution; (4) Evaluate(ctx context.Context, contract *ScenarioContract, workDir string) ([]ContractFailure, error) method: for each scenario's assertions, evaluate all 5 types — file_exists (os.Stat), file_contains (os.ReadFile + strings.Contains), file_not_modified (git diff --name-only HEAD -- <path>, empty output means unmodified), file_not_exists (os.Stat negated), file_not_contains (os.ReadFile + !strings.Contains). Check ALL assertions per scenario (no short-circuit). Each ContractAssertion must have exactly one field set; zero or multiple fields set returns an error. Paths are joined with workDir.

Create internal/next/contract/evaluator_test.go with tests for FileSystemEvaluator. Use a real temp directory (t.TempDir()) for filesystem assertions. Mock the git runner via a constructor parameter or function field. Tests: (1) TestEvaluate_FileExists_Pass and _Fail; (2) TestEvaluate_FileContains_Pass and _Fail with correct failure message format 'contract:<name> — file_contains failed: ...'; (3) TestEvaluate_FileNotExists_Pass and _Fail; (4) TestEvaluate_FileNotContains_Pass and _Fail; (5) TestEvaluate_FileNotModified_Pass (mock git returns empty) and _Fail (mock git returns filename); (6) TestEvaluate_EmptyAssertions returns no failures; (7) TestEvaluate_MultipleAssertionsPartialFailure: 2 assertions, one passes, one fails — both evaluated, only failure returned; (8) ContractFailure format uses em-dash separator: 'contract:<scenario-name> — <assertion-type> failed: <details>'.

Add ContractsWritten bool field with json tag 'contracts_written' to the RunState struct in internal/next/runstore/types.go. Place it logically near other stage-completion flags (e.g., near FinalValidationPassed). Do NOT add it to any per-cycle reset logic. Confirm internal/next/specloop/specloop.go does NOT reset ContractsWritten — read the file and verify the cycle-reset block (around line 42-50) does not reference ContractsWritten.

Add ContractsWrittenEvent and ContractsBlockedEvent types to internal/next/runstore/events.go following the existing pattern. ContractsWrittenEvent embeds BaseEvent and has ScenarioCount int json:'scenario_count'. ContractsBlockedEvent embeds BaseEvent and has Reason string json:'reason'. Register both in the unmarshalEvent switch with type strings 'contracts_written' and 'contracts_blocked'. The BaseEvent Type field should be set to the correct string in each event.

Create internal/next/specloop/stages/write_contracts.go implementing the WriteContracts stage. Include: (1) ContractWriter interface: WriteContracts(ctx context.Context, scenarios []contract.SpecScenario, specPacket string) (*contract.ScenarioContract, error); (2) WriteContractsStageConfig struct: Store runstore.Store, SpecPath string, EvidenceDir string; (3) WriteContractsStage struct with contractWriter ContractWriter, cfg WriteContractsStageConfig, eventLog *runstore.EventLog, budget interface with HardBudgetExceeded() bool; (4) NewWriteContractsStage constructor; (5) Name() returns 'write_contracts'; (6) Run(ctx, rs) logic: if rs.ContractsWritten return Continue; read spec file at cfg.SpecPath, call contract.ParseScenarios; if no scenarios return Continue; if budget exhausted return Blocked; attempt LLM invocation up to 3 times (max 2 retries): on each attempt call contractWriter.WriteContracts, validate YAML parseability and vocabulary (each ContractAssertion has exactly 1 field set using known keys), retry on failure passing error context; after 3 failures emit contracts_blocked event and return Blocked; on success: marshal to YAML, write to cfg.EvidenceDir/scenario-contracts.yaml, set rs.ContractsWritten=true, emit contracts_written event with scenario count, return Continue. Model tier: Sonnet (P1).

Create internal/next/specloop/stages/write_contracts_test.go with unit tests using a mock ContractWriter. Tests: (1) TestWriteContracts_HappyPath: valid scenarios in spec, writer returns valid contract, file written to EvidenceDir, rs.ContractsWritten=true, contracts_written event emitted with correct scenario count; (2) TestWriteContracts_Idempotent: rs.ContractsWritten=true on entry → immediate Continue, contractWriter never called; (3) TestWriteContracts_NoScenarios: spec file has no '### Scenario:' sections → Continue, no file written, writer never called; (4) TestWriteContracts_InvalidYAML: writer returns non-YAML string 3 times → Blocked, contracts_blocked event emitted; (5) TestWriteContracts_UnknownVocabularyKey: writer returns valid YAML with unknown assertion key (e.g., 'status: completed') 3 times → Blocked; (6) TestWriteContracts_BudgetExhausted: budget exhausted before invocation → Blocked immediately, writer not called. Use t.TempDir() for EvidenceDir.

Extend internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go: (1) Add ContractEvaluator interface: Evaluate(ctx context.Context, contract *contract.ScenarioContract, workDir string) ([]contract.ContractFailure, error); (2) Add EvidenceDir string and Evaluator ContractEvaluator fields to ValidateStageConfig; (3) Update ValidateStage struct to store cfg including new fields; (4) In Run(): if cfg.Evaluator != nil and cfg.EvidenceDir != empty, check for scenario-contracts.yaml in EvidenceDir — if file does not exist, skip silently (not a failure); if file exists, parse YAML into ScenarioContract, call Evaluator.Evaluate(ctx, contract, workDir), convert each ContractFailure to failure string using format 'contract:<ScenarioName> — <AssertionType> failed: <Details>' and append to failures slice; run shell checks afterward regardless; combine all failures before deciding next action. Import internal/next/contract package for types.

Extend internal/next/specloop/stages/validate_test.go with contract evaluation tests using a mock ContractEvaluator. Tests: (1) TestValidate_ContractFailure: mock evaluator returns one ContractFailure, result is ReplanFrom with failure string matching 'contract:<name> — <type> failed: <details>'; (2) TestValidate_ContractAndShellBothFail: mock evaluator returns a failure AND shell validator fails — both failures appear in the replan context; (3) TestValidate_ContractFileMissing: EvidenceDir set but no scenario-contracts.yaml file present — no failure, evaluator not called; (4) TestValidate_ContractPassShellFail: contracts pass but shell validator fails — replan context contains only shell failure; (5) TestValidate_NilEvaluator: Evaluator field nil in config — no contract check, existing behavior unchanged. Use t.TempDir() for EvidenceDir when contract file present.

Create internal/next/contract/llm_writer.go with an LLM-backed ContractWriter implementation. The struct (e.g., LLMContractWriter) takes an llmadapter.LLMAdapter, formats a prompt instructing the LLM to translate the provided SpecScenarios and spec packet into a ScenarioContract YAML using only the valid vocabulary (file_exists, file_contains, file_not_modified, file_not_exists, file_not_contains), and parses the LLM response as YAML into *ScenarioContract. On error context retry, include the previous error in the prompt. Uses Sonnet (P1) tier. Then update cmd/gromit-next/stage_provider.go: (1) add noopContractWriter struct implementing ContractWriter with WriteContracts returning empty ScenarioContract; (2) construct writeContractsStage in BuildStages after planStage and before executeStage, using LLMContractWriter when provider available else noopContractWriter, passing store, cfg.SpecPath, and evidenceDir; (3) update validateStage construction to pass EvidenceDir and Evaluator (contract.NewFileSystemEvaluator(workDir)) in ValidateStageConfig. Import internal/next/contract package.

Create internal/next/specloop/contract_integration_test.go with //go:build integration tag in the specloop package. Tests exercise the WriteContracts → Validate pipeline using the scenarioStage pattern from existing integration tests (no real LLM). (1) TestIntegration_ContractFailureTriggersReplan: build a pipeline with a writeContracts scenarioStage that sets rs.ContractsWritten=true and writes a scenario-contracts.yaml with a file_contains assertion to a temp EvidenceDir, an execute scenarioStage that is a no-op (file never created), a ValidateStage with a real FileSystemEvaluator pointing at a temp workdir — Validate fails with 'contract:...' failure, replan triggered, second cycle WriteContracts is no-op (ContractsWritten=true), execute creates the file, Validate passes; (2) TestIntegration_ContractsPreservedAcrossReplan: on replan cycle, writeContracts stage never re-runs (ContractsWritten flag preserved), pipeline completes; (3) TestIntegration_NoContractFileSkipped: no scenario-contracts.yaml in EvidenceDir, ValidateStage with Evaluator skips silently, pipeline continues. Run with go test -tags integration.

Fix TestRunSpecTestEnvRestoresWorkingDirectory to handle macOS symlink path resolution. The test fails because os.Getwd() after os.Chdir() returns the canonical /private/var/folders/... path while originalWD holds the symlinked /var/folders/... path. Resolve both paths via filepath.EvalSymlinks before comparing in the test at cmd/gromit/run_spec_flag_test.go:116-121.

Fix TestDebugCompatibilityDiagnostics_CommandSurfaceSupportsLegacyAndExplicitConfig: replace relative fixture path with resolveProjectPath to prevent CWD-contamination from t.Chdir() in concurrent tests

blocker_summary: review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate_test.go:143 — The new Validate tests cover: contract failure, combined contract+shell failure, missing contract file, contracts pass/shell fail, and nil evaluator. Missing test: what happens when the contract file exists but contains invalid YAML (yaml.Unmarshal returns error). The spec requires that if the file exists but is unparseable, Validate returns an error — this path is exercised by the validate.go code but has no corresponding test. (suggested fix: Add TestValidate_MalformedContractFile: write a scenario-contracts.yaml containing invalid YAML bytes to the temp dir, run the stage, and assert that Run returns a non-nil error (not a ReplanFrom action).)
replan_context: review:code_quality:error:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:90 — FinalValidationResultEvent emits Passed: result.Pass (shell-only), but the stage now returns ReplanFrom when contracts fail even if result.Pass is true. Any observer reading this event will see Passed:true for a cycle that is actually replanning due to contract failures. (suggested fix: Determine the combined pass state before emitting the event. Compute a local `overallPass := result.Pass && len(failures) == 0` after all failures are collected, then emit `Passed: overallPass`. Alternatively, move the event emission after the combined pass check, emitting it only on the Continue path, to avoid the race between shell-result and contract-result.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:53 — rs.LastValidationResult is set to fmt.Sprintf("pass=%v", result.Pass) — shell-only — before contract failures are evaluated. If contracts fail but shell passes, the stored summary says "pass=true" while the stage returns ReplanFrom. EvidenceStage or any other downstream reader will misread the run outcome. (suggested fix: Set rs.LastValidationResult after all failures (contract + shell) are collected and the combined pass decision is known. Or include contract failure count in the summary: e.g., fmt.Sprintf("pass=%v contractFailures=%d", result.Pass && len(contractFailures)==0, len(contractFailures)).)

review:code_quality:warning:cmd/gromit-next/stage_provider.go:123 — The contract writer adapter uses policy.Models.Evaluator as its tier, but the spec (spec 0002e §Architecture) states WriteContracts must use Sonnet / P1, which corresponds to policy.Models.Planner. The comment 'Sonnet / P1 tier via evaluator tier' asserts they are equivalent, but nothing in the policy schema enforces this — Evaluator could be configured as Haiku or Opus. (suggested fix: Use policy.Models.Planner (not policy.Models.Evaluator) for both the adapter Config.Tier and the fallback tier argument, matching the spec's P1 requirement. Update the comment accordingly.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:61 — The filename "scenario-contracts.yaml" is a raw string literal with no corresponding package-level constant. The WriteContracts stage will independently hardcode the same string. Two places in separate packages owning the same magic string is a maintenance hazard — a rename in one place silently breaks the other. (suggested fix: Define a package-level (or cross-package) constant, e.g. const ContractFileName = "scenario-contracts.yaml" in internal/next/contract/, and import it in both validate.go and the WriteContracts stage.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:54 — ValidateStage.Run() performs direct file I/O (os.Stat, os.ReadFile) and YAML unmarshaling (yaml.Unmarshal) inline. This adds two new import dependencies ("os", "gopkg.in/yaml.v3") to a stage that previously had none, and couples the orchestration layer to file-parsing concerns. The ContractEvaluator interface was designed as an injection point; the file loading should live at that boundary. (suggested fix: Either (a) change ContractEvaluator.Evaluate to accept the contract file path instead of a parsed *ScenarioContract, letting the evaluator implementation handle loading/parsing; or (b) introduce a small unexported helper loadContractFile(path string) (*contract.ScenarioContract, error) to isolate the I/O so the Run method body stays at the orchestration level.)

review:spec_alignment:error:internal/next/specloop/stages/write_contracts.go:0 — File does not exist. The diff references `stages.NewWriteContractsStage`, `stages.ContractWriter`, and `stages.WriteContractsStageConfig` in stage_provider.go, but no file in the stages package defines these. The code will not compile. Missing: WriteContractsStage struct and Run method, ContractWriter interface, WriteContractsStageConfig type, NewWriteContractsStage constructor, idempotency check (rs.ContractsWritten), budget check before LLM invocation, 3-attempt retry logic, vocabulary validation, event emission (contracts_written / contracts_blocked), empty-scenarios no-op path, rs.ContractsWritten = true on success. (suggested fix: Create internal/next/specloop/stages/write_contracts.go implementing the ContractWriter interface, WriteContractsStageConfig, and WriteContractsStage with all behaviours specified in the Architecture section: idempotency via rs.ContractsWritten, single-batch LLM invocation, vocabulary validation with 2 retries (3 total attempts), budget check before invocation, event emission, and early return on empty scenarios.)

review:spec_alignment:error:internal/next/contract/:0 — The internal/next/contract/ package does not exist in the codebase, yet it is imported by both validate.go (line 6) and stage_provider.go (line 11). The code will not compile. Missing: SpecScenario type, ScenarioContract type, ScenarioAssertions type, ContractAssertion type, FileContainsAssertion type, ContractFailure type, ParseScenarios function, NewFileSystemEvaluator constructor (all five assertion evaluators: file_exists, file_contains, file_not_modified, file_not_exists, file_not_contains), NewLLMContractWriter constructor. The SpecScenario type and ParseScenarios function must be exported for reuse by spec 0002f (AC17). (suggested fix: Create the internal/next/contract/ package with all types defined in the spec's Key types section. Implement FileSystemEvaluator.Evaluate checking each assertion type using strings.Contains for file_contains/file_not_contains and git diff --name-only HEAD for file_not_modified. Implement LLMContractWriter.WriteContracts wrapping the llmadapter. Implement ParseScenarios to match ### Scenario: headers extracting Given/When/Then/Notes blocks, skipping scenarios missing When or Then.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:54 — Contract evaluation block reads and parses scenario-contracts.yaml directly with yaml.Unmarshal rather than delegating file I/O to the ContractEvaluator. The spec defines ContractEvaluator.Evaluate(ctx, *ScenarioContract, workDir) — the caller is responsible for locating and loading the file, but the evaluator only receives an already-parsed ScenarioContract. This split is correct per the spec, however the file I/O (os.Stat, os.ReadFile, yaml.Unmarshal) inside ValidateStage.Run makes the stage harder to unit-test for file-read errors. Not a correctness defect but note that tests for YAML parse errors within Validate are absent. (suggested fix: Add a unit test covering the case where scenario-contracts.yaml exists but contains invalid YAML — verify that ValidateStage.Run returns an error (not silently continues). This exercises the yaml.Unmarshal error path introduced at validate.go:67.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:cmd/gromit-next/stage_provider.go:121 — Contract writer adapter is constructed with policy.Models.Evaluator tier (currently maps to 'high' → 'sonnet') with the comment 'Sonnet / P1 tier via evaluator tier'. The spec requires Sonnet (P1) for WriteContracts (AC15). This happens to be correct because policy.Models.Evaluator = 'high' → 'sonnet' per the current execpolicy mapping, but the tier selection is implicit. If the Evaluator tier is ever changed (e.g., upgraded to Opus for acceptance evaluation), the contract writer would silently change model without any indication in the code. (suggested fix: Use policy.Models.Planner (also 'high' → 'sonnet') for the contract adapter, since WriteContracts is a translation task analogous to planning — or add an explicit Models.ContractWriter field in execpolicy.Models initialized to 'high'. Add a comment explaining why this tier is intentional, not inherited from evaluator semantics.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate_test.go:143 — The new Validate tests cover: contract failure, combined contract+shell failure, missing contract file, contracts pass/shell fail, and nil evaluator. Missing test: what happens when the contract file exists but contains invalid YAML (yaml.Unmarshal returns error). The spec requires that if the file exists but is unparseable, Validate returns an error — this path is exercised by the validate.go code but has no corresponding test. (suggested fix: Add TestValidate_MalformedContractFile: write a scenario-contracts.yaml containing invalid YAML bytes to the temp dir, run the stage, and assert that Run returns a non-nil error (not a ReplanFrom action).)

review_findings: review:code_quality:error:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:90 — FinalValidationResultEvent emits Passed: result.Pass (shell-only), but the stage now returns ReplanFrom when contracts fail even if result.Pass is true. Any observer reading this event will see Passed:true for a cycle that is actually replanning due to contract failures. (suggested fix: Determine the combined pass state before emitting the event. Compute a local `overallPass := result.Pass && len(failures) == 0` after all failures are collected, then emit `Passed: overallPass`. Alternatively, move the event emission after the combined pass check, emitting it only on the Continue path, to avoid the race between shell-result and contract-result.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:53 — rs.LastValidationResult is set to fmt.Sprintf("pass=%v", result.Pass) — shell-only — before contract failures are evaluated. If contracts fail but shell passes, the stored summary says "pass=true" while the stage returns ReplanFrom. EvidenceStage or any other downstream reader will misread the run outcome. (suggested fix: Set rs.LastValidationResult after all failures (contract + shell) are collected and the combined pass decision is known. Or include contract failure count in the summary: e.g., fmt.Sprintf("pass=%v contractFailures=%d", result.Pass && len(contractFailures)==0, len(contractFailures)).)

review:code_quality:warning:cmd/gromit-next/stage_provider.go:123 — The contract writer adapter uses policy.Models.Evaluator as its tier, but the spec (spec 0002e §Architecture) states WriteContracts must use Sonnet / P1, which corresponds to policy.Models.Planner. The comment 'Sonnet / P1 tier via evaluator tier' asserts they are equivalent, but nothing in the policy schema enforces this — Evaluator could be configured as Haiku or Opus. (suggested fix: Use policy.Models.Planner (not policy.Models.Evaluator) for both the adapter Config.Tier and the fallback tier argument, matching the spec's P1 requirement. Update the comment accordingly.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:61 — The filename "scenario-contracts.yaml" is a raw string literal with no corresponding package-level constant. The WriteContracts stage will independently hardcode the same string. Two places in separate packages owning the same magic string is a maintenance hazard — a rename in one place silently breaks the other. (suggested fix: Define a package-level (or cross-package) constant, e.g. const ContractFileName = "scenario-contracts.yaml" in internal/next/contract/, and import it in both validate.go and the WriteContracts stage.)

review:code_quality:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:54 — ValidateStage.Run() performs direct file I/O (os.Stat, os.ReadFile) and YAML unmarshaling (yaml.Unmarshal) inline. This adds two new import dependencies ("os", "gopkg.in/yaml.v3") to a stage that previously had none, and couples the orchestration layer to file-parsing concerns. The ContractEvaluator interface was designed as an injection point; the file loading should live at that boundary. (suggested fix: Either (a) change ContractEvaluator.Evaluate to accept the contract file path instead of a parsed *ScenarioContract, letting the evaluator implementation handle loading/parsing; or (b) introduce a small unexported helper loadContractFile(path string) (*contract.ScenarioContract, error) to isolate the I/O so the Run method body stays at the orchestration level.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate.go:54 — Contract evaluation block reads and parses scenario-contracts.yaml directly with yaml.Unmarshal rather than delegating file I/O to the ContractEvaluator. The spec defines ContractEvaluator.Evaluate(ctx, *ScenarioContract, workDir) — the caller is responsible for locating and loading the file, but the evaluator only receives an already-parsed ScenarioContract. This split is correct per the spec, however the file I/O (os.Stat, os.ReadFile, yaml.Unmarshal) inside ValidateStage.Run makes the stage harder to unit-test for file-read errors. Not a correctness defect but note that tests for YAML parse errors within Validate are absent. (suggested fix: Add a unit test covering the case where scenario-contracts.yaml exists but contains invalid YAML — verify that ValidateStage.Run returns an error (not silently continues). This exercises the yaml.Unmarshal error path introduced at validate.go:67.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:cmd/gromit-next/stage_provider.go:121 — Contract writer adapter is constructed with policy.Models.Evaluator tier (currently maps to 'high' → 'sonnet') with the comment 'Sonnet / P1 tier via evaluator tier'. The spec requires Sonnet (P1) for WriteContracts (AC15). This happens to be correct because policy.Models.Evaluator = 'high' → 'sonnet' per the current execpolicy mapping, but the tier selection is implicit. If the Evaluator tier is ever changed (e.g., upgraded to Opus for acceptance evaluation), the contract writer would silently change model without any indication in the code. (suggested fix: Use policy.Models.Planner (also 'high' → 'sonnet') for the contract adapter, since WriteContracts is a translation task analogous to planning — or add an explicit Models.ContractWriter field in execpolicy.Models initialized to 'high'. Add a comment explaining why this tier is intentional, not inherited from evaluator semantics.)

review:spec_alignment:warning:internal/next/specloop/stages/validate_test.go:143 — The new Validate tests cover: contract failure, combined contract+shell failure, missing contract file, contracts pass/shell fail, and nil evaluator.
